title: Claude Code for Beginners Tutorial [Full Course]
author: freeCodeCamp.org
summary: A long, structured course that puts Claude Code into a normal development workflow. It starts with a new project and then moves to a real multi-file codebase, so you see both the easy case and the hard one. freeCodeCamp keeps the pace slow and shows every command, which makes it good to follow along with a keyboard.
who_for: A working developer who wants one complete, ordered pass over Claude Code instead of twenty short clips.
skip_if: Skip if you already run Claude Code daily. The first two hours cover install, permissions, and basic prompting, and you will only get the last part of value for four and a half hours of time.

title: Claude Code Tutorial - Build Apps 10x Faster with AI
author: Programming with Mosh
summary: Mosh builds one real app (an expense tracker) from a starter repo and uses Claude Code the way an engineer would: read the code first, plan, then change small pieces. The teaching is very clean and the GitHub repo lets you code along. It is the best single hour if you want habits, not tricks.
who_for: Developers who have installed Claude Code but still treat it like a chat box and get messy results.
skip_if: Skip if you want MCP, subagents, or hooks. This stays on core coding work and does not touch the extension layer.

title: Claude Code Crash Course For Developers
author: Traversy Media
summary: A fast, no-padding starting point from a channel with a long record of accurate web-dev teaching. Brad Traversy shares his prompt gist in the description, so you leave with text you can reuse instead of only notes. Good density for the running time.
who_for: Experienced web developers who want the whole tool explained once, quickly, and then to get back to work.
skip_if: Skip if you are new to the terminal or to git. The pace assumes you already know your stack and only need the Claude Code part.
notes: 172,346 views, 1:03:23, verified 2026-08-22; contains sponsor and affiliate links in the description

title: Complete Claude Code Course In 2 Hours For Developers
author: Krish Naik
summary: Krish Naik covers Claude Code across all four surfaces: terminal, IDE, desktop app, and browser. He explains how the agent reads a codebase, edits files, and runs commands, and he keeps a Python and data slant that suits analysts as much as app developers.
who_for: Python and data people who want a full course from a teacher used to explaining tooling to that audience.
skip_if: Skip if you want polished production and tight editing. The delivery is live and repeats itself, so two hours holds about ninety minutes of content.

title: CLAUDE CODE Full Course For Beginners (DATA DOMAIN Edition)
author: Ansh Lamba
summary: The only long Claude Code course we found that is written for data work instead of app building. It goes from setup through skills, MCP, hooks, scheduling, context control, plugins, and the marketplace, with data examples all the way. Nearly seven hours, so treat it as a course, not a video.
who_for: Data analysts and data engineers who want the full Claude Code feature set explained with data problems, not to-do apps.
skip_if: Skip if you only have one evening. At 6:47 it needs a real schedule, and a shorter course will teach you the same basics faster.
notes: 154,192 views, 6:47:47, verified 2026-08-22; five months old, so check the plugin and marketplace sections against current docs

title: My Claude Code Workflow for 2026
author: Ray Amjad
summary: One engineer shows his complete daily setup end to end: how he opens a task, what he puts in configuration, and where he stops the agent and takes over. Watching a full real workflow is more useful than a feature list, and the creator states he takes no sponsors, so the opinions are his own.
who_for: Developers who know the commands but have not settled on a repeatable way of working.
skip_if: Skip if you want step-by-step instruction. This is one person's opinion of a good setup, not a tutorial you can copy line by line.
notes: 27,271 views, 20:26, verified 2026-08-22; published January 2026, so some menus have changed

title: How I use Claude Code for real engineering
author: Matt Pocock
summary: The clearest short explanation of plan mode we found. Matt Pocock dictates a rough prompt, lets Claude explore the codebase and ask questions, then splits the job into phases that survive across several context windows. He also shows the rules file that keeps plans short.
who_for: Developers whose Claude Code sessions fall apart on anything bigger than a single file.
skip_if: Skip if you want a hands-on build. It is a walkthrough of a way of thinking, and at ten minutes it explains more than it demonstrates.
notes: 292,912 views, 10:11, verified 2026-08-22; from October 2025, so the interface looks older than today, but the plan-mode method still holds

title: Red Green Refactor is OP With Claude Code
author: Matt Pocock
summary: Five minutes on why test-driven development is the best control on a coding agent. A failing test gives Claude a target it cannot argue with, so the loop ends when the test passes instead of when you get tired. Short, sharp, and immediately usable.
who_for: Developers who let Claude write code first and then find they cannot tell whether it works.
skip_if: Skip if you do not already know how to write a test in your language. The video assumes the red-green-refactor cycle and only adds the agent part.

title: Claude Code Task System: ANTI-HYPE Agentic Coding (Advanced)
author: IndyDevDan
summary: A close look at how Claude Code breaks work into tasks and hands them to agents, and how to shape that instead of fighting it. IndyDevDan builds against real code and argues from measured results rather than excitement, which is rare in this topic.
who_for: Builders who already orchestrate agents and want to understand the layer under the commands.
skip_if: Skip if you have not used subagents yet. The video starts where most tutorials end and will not slow down for you.
notes: 47,381 views, 28:26, verified 2026-08-22; the creator promotes his own paid course in the description

title: Parallel Claude Code + Git Worktrees: This Setup Will Change How You Ship
author: Cole Medin
summary: Cole Medin runs three to ten Claude Code agents at the same time and shows the full setup that keeps them from overwriting each other. The argument is that output comes from workflow shape, not from better prompts. Practical, with the branch and review steps included.
who_for: Developers who have more independent tasks than they have time, and who are comfortable with git branches.
skip_if: Skip if you work on one feature at a time. Running many agents adds review load, and with a single task it costs you more than it saves.

title: Git Worktrees Explained — Run Multiple AI Agents in Parallel (Claude Code Tutorial)
author: bri
summary: A focused explainer on git worktrees themselves: one repository, several isolated working directories, each on its own branch with its own Claude Code session. If the parallel-agent videos lost you at the git part, start here instead.
who_for: Developers who understand branches but have never used worktrees and want the mechanism before the workflow.
skip_if: Skip if you already use worktrees. Most of the twenty minutes explains the git feature, not the Claude Code part.

title: Completely understand hooks in less than 20 minutes
author: Burke Holland
summary: Builds hooks from nothing: the JSON file, the bash script it calls, and how to debug it when it stays silent. It also names the one hook event that covers most needs, which saves you from writing five. Ends with a working example, not a diagram.
who_for: Developers who want the agent to run a formatter, a linter, or a guard automatically, every time, with no prompting.
skip_if: Skip if you do not write shell scripts. Every example is a bash file, and without that you cannot use any of it.
notes: 33,394 views, 19:30, verified 2026-08-22; covers both GitHub Copilot and Claude Code hooks, so part of it is not about Claude

title: Hooks in Claude Code — Full Theory + Practical Use | CampusX
author: CampusX
summary: The deepest free explanation of hooks we found. It covers the internal shape of Claude Code first (the coding harness, the agent loop, the session lifecycle) and only then shows hooks as the way to force fixed behaviour on a model that is not fixed. Good for people who want to know why, not only how.
who_for: Developers who need to stop an agent from doing certain things, and who want the reason behind each hook event.
skip_if: Skip if you just want a working hook today. The first half is architecture, and you will wait a long time for the file you can copy.

title: Claude Code Headless Automation & Agent Workflows
author: ExamPro
summary: Takes Claude Code out of the terminal and puts it in a pipeline: headless runs, GitHub Actions, and CI/CD steps that no human watches. This is the part most tutorials skip, and it is what you need before you let an agent touch a shared repository.
who_for: Developers and DevOps people who want Claude to run on a trigger, not on a person typing.
skip_if: Skip if you have no CI system. Without a pipeline to put it in, headless mode has nowhere to go.
notes: 14,145 views, 27:48, verified 2026-08-22; one free lesson from a paid ExamPro course, and the description sells that course

title: Claude Code Sub-Agents: Step-by-Step Beginner Tutorial
author: Thetips4you
summary: A patient, hands-on build of three subagents that work together on one Python project. It shows both ways to make them, through the /agents command and by writing the file yourself, then runs them so you can see the handoff. Good first contact with the idea.
who_for: Developers who have read about subagents and now want to make three that actually run.
skip_if: Skip if you already write agent definition files. The pace is slow and there is nothing here about limiting tools or designing output formats.

title: Stop Confusing Skills and Subagents in Claude Code (Watch This)
author: TechWhistle
summary: Answers the question everyone asks after their first week: skills or subagents, and when. The model it gives (skills are recipes, subagents are cooks) is simple and it holds up, and the video then shows four real patterns including putting skills inside subagents.
who_for: Anyone who keeps building the wrong one of the two and cannot say why the result was wrong.
skip_if: Skip if you want build instructions. It sorts out the concepts in nine minutes and leaves the typing to you.

title: Claude Code Skills + Subagents: Build a Security Scanner
author: Leon van Zyl
summary: Skills and subagents applied to one real job: a scanner that looks for OWASP Top 10 problems, with broken access control as the worked example. Building something with a right answer is a much better test of the feature than another to-do list.
who_for: Developers who learn by building one complete thing and who care about security review.
skip_if: Skip if you do not know the OWASP Top 10. The video explains the Claude parts, not the vulnerabilities.
notes: 10,847 views, 13:44, verified 2026-08-22; the creator links his paid community in the description

title: 8 Claude Code Skills Every Developer Needs in 2026
author: Eric Tech
summary: The title reads like a listicle, but each of the eight items is a skill the creator runs on his own product, shown live in the editor. The strongest parts are the TDD pipeline (brainstorm, plan, test, execute) and the skill that writes other skills. Copy the patterns, not the list.
who_for: Developers who have made one skill and now want to see what good ones look like at work.
skip_if: Skip if you have not made a skill yet. It shows finished skills running and does not teach you the file format from zero.
notes: 11,395 views, 32:52, verified 2026-08-22; the creator demonstrates on his own commercial product

title: How Model Context Protocol (MCP) actually works
author: Google Cloud Tech
summary: Eight minutes that explain the actual problem MCP solves: normal APIs are built for programs that follow rules, and models do not. Clear diagrams, no product pitch, and vendor-neutral even though Google made it. The best short answer to what MCP is.
who_for: Developers who keep hearing MCP and want the concept right before they build or install anything.
skip_if: Skip if you want to write an MCP server today. There is no code and no setup, only the model of how it works.
notes: 280,692 views, 7:58, verified 2026-08-22; the examples link to Google Cloud tools, but the protocol content is generic

title: MCP Tutorial for Beginners: Connect Claude to Any Tool (2026)
author: Thetips4you
summary: Goes from nothing to a working MCP server in Python, with no paid API key needed to follow along. The pace is slow on purpose and every file is shown, so it suits people who have never written a server before.
who_for: Developers and analysts who want their own first MCP server running on their own machine tonight.
skip_if: Skip if you write servers already. It spends most of the time on Python basics and setup, and covers nothing about remote hosting or authentication.

title: Build an MCP Server from Scratch in 2026 | Local, Remote, OAuth & Claude Skills
author: Code With Antonio
summary: The most complete free MCP build we found. It covers local servers, remote servers, OAuth, and how skills and CLIs sit around one shared core so the same code serves several clients. Source code is linked. Nearly four hours, and every hour earns its place.
who_for: Builders who need to ship an MCP server that other people will connect to, not a demo on localhost.
skip_if: Skip if you only want to install existing MCP servers. This is a production build with auth and deployment, and it is far more than a user needs.
notes: 77,394 views, 3:52:40, verified 2026-08-22; the description carries affiliate links to Clerk and Railway

title: Claude Agent SDK [Full Workshop] — Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic
author: AI Engineer
summary: A conference workshop given by the engineer who works on the SDK, recorded by the AI Engineer channel. It starts with what an agent actually is and then goes into the architecture and the code. Depth you normally pay for, on a channel with a strong record for technical talks.
who_for: Developers putting Claude agents inside their own product and needing the design reasoning, not only the API calls.
skip_if: Skip if you use Claude Code and have no plan to write software around it. This is SDK work and expects you to be comfortable in Python or TypeScript.
notes: 145,206 views, 1:52:25, verified 2026-08-22; recorded January 2026, so check current SDK method names against the docs

title: You Can Build The Craziest Things with Claudes Agent SDK
author: Traversy Media
summary: A short crash course on putting Claude Code inside your own application through the Agent SDK. It answers the first question everyone has, which is what the SDK gives you that the raw API does not, and it does that in fifteen minutes.
who_for: Developers deciding whether to use the Agent SDK or call the Messages API themselves.
skip_if: Skip if you already decided to use the SDK. Watch the AI Engineer workshop instead, because this one stops before the hard parts.
notes: 53,910 views, 14:25, verified 2026-08-22; sponsored segment in the video

title: I Built an Agentic Software Factory with Codex and Claude Code
author: Owain Lewis
summary: A full pipeline shown on a real open-source Rust project: agents poll GitHub for labelled issues, refine the ticket, write the change, run tests and review, then open a pull request with nobody at the terminal. It is the honest version of automated development, including where it breaks.
who_for: Builders who want to see what unattended agent work really looks like before they try it on their own repository.
skip_if: Skip if you are still learning Claude Code basics. This assumes CI, GitHub automation, and a review process you already trust.
notes: 45,403 views, 20:49, verified 2026-08-22; uses OpenAI Codex alongside Claude Code, so part of the pipeline is not Claude

title: How I Use Claude Code as a Data Analyst (10 Real Use Cases)
author: Ryan & Matt Data Science
summary: Ten analyst jobs done on screen, not described: cleaning, joining, checking, and reporting. It is one of the few Claude Code videos that treats a dataset as the subject instead of a web app, so the prompts and file layouts transfer straight to analyst work.
who_for: Data analysts who use Claude in chat and want to move to the terminal where the files actually live.
skip_if: Skip if you have never used a command line. The video assumes you can already run Python from a terminal and navigate folders.
notes: 41,019 views, 58:36, verified 2026-08-22; the description promotes the creators' paid community and consulting
